title: Describe a task with a class

outcomes.can: Predict what two variables for one object share.
Say which code may change a property, and read the error when other code tries.
Write a class with a constructor, properties and methods.
Return a new object and leave the one you were given unchanged.

intro: A class groups data with the methods that work on it. This module covers properties, constructors and instance methods, and what happens when two variables refer to the same object.

steps.title: A class is a blueprint
steps.text: A class describes one kind of thing. new TaskCard("Pack", 30) creates an object from it. A property is a named value on each object. public string Title { get; private set; } can be read by any code and changed only inside the class. public int Minutes { get; } can be set only in the constructor. A property can also work out its value each time it is read: public bool Long => Minutes > 60;. The constructor has the same name as the class. It runs once, when the object is created, and gives the properties their first values. A method without static belongs to one object and uses that object's own properties.

steps.title: Two names, one object
steps.text: same is assigned from card, then the card is renamed through same. Predict the first line of output.

steps.title: Follow the reference
steps.text: TaskCard same = card; does not copy the object. A class variable holds a reference to an object, and the assignment copies that reference. card and same now refer to one object, so a change made through same is visible through card. This differs from int, where assignment copies the number itself. Describe then reads the current Title and Minutes of that one object.

steps.title: Change a get-only property
steps.text: Line 2 assigns to a property that has only get. Read the example before checking.

steps.title: Read the compiler error
steps.text: Check the example. CS0200 says the property cannot be assigned because it is read only. Minutes has no set, so only the constructor can give it a value. This is deliberate: the class decides which changes are allowed, and other code has to go through its methods.

steps.title: Finish the board
steps.text: The starter has the properties and the constructor. Fill in the two empty methods.

steps.title: Write a task card
steps.text: Work from the prompt. The starter has the member names, and the bodies are yours.

questions.prompt: What is the first line of output?

choices.feedback: same and card refer to the same object, so the rename is visible through card.
Assigning a class variable copies the reference, not the object. Both names see the rename.
The first print shows only the Title. Describe is called on the next line.

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.text: The compiler reports an error on line 2.
choices.feedback: Minutes has only get, so code outside the constructor cannot assign to it (CS0200).
Minutes has no set. The compiler rejects the assignment.

choices.text: It prints 30, because the assignment is ignored.
choices.feedback: An assignment that is not allowed is a compile error. It is never silently skipped.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise one member form each. They do not check a sequence of calls on one object.
